North Dakota State Parcel Program
Maintaining an accurate and publicly accessible Statewide Parcel Dataset through a partnership with North Dakota Counties and their vendors .
About the Program
The goal of the State Parcel Program is to maintain an accurate, publicly accessible, maintained, Statewide Parcel Dataset that supports the State of North Dakota business needs. Local governments are and will remain as the primary custodians of their parcel data.
The State Parcel Program began as the Statewide Parcel Project and was funded by the 66th Legislative Assembly, appropriating funds through House Bill 1021. During the 2019-2021 Biennium, AppGeo aggregated parcel boundary and tax roll data from 51 counties and developed parcel boundary data for Adams and Benson counties.
Beginning with the 2021-2023 Biennium, the Statewide Parcel Dataset began to be maintained on a regular basis as part of the GIS Program and leveraging the existing North Dakota GIS Hub infrastructure. Data maintenance consists of parcel boundary and tax roll data being voluntarily submitted by counties and their vendors via uploading and/or harvesting by the GIS Hub. The frequency of data updates varies by county, ranging from weekly to yearly. Consider reviewing the "Date Imported" field in the parcel and tax roll data and then if needed, contact the county to inquire if there are more recent data not yet submitted to the Statewide Parcel Dataset.

Accessing and Using the Parcel Data
Data Access - Viewing
The North Dakota Parcel Viewer provides the ability for viewing the Statewide Parcel Dataset and as a means to communicate data-related questions. Please note that the data in the North Dakota Parcel Viewer is updated weekly.
The Statewide Parcel Dataset can also be viewed within the GIS Hub Data Portal by first searching or browsing for the parcel data as outlined below in the 'Data Access - Download' section. Once the parcel boundary or tax roll data has been selected, the data will be displayed.
In addition to viewing the Statewide Parcel Dataset within the North Dakota Parcel Viewer and the GIS Hub Data Portal, the data can also be accessed and viewed using desktop and web applications by streaming the data via a connection to the data or by downloading the data. Please see the next two sections for this information.
North Dakota Parcel Viewer
Data Access - Connect
North Dakota state agency GIS users can connect to the parcel data on the GIS Hub's "hub" enterprise geodatabase using ArcGIS Pro, selecting the ' Parcels ' feature class . This access method works well when working in an agency office and using a state-provided network connection.
All GIS users can connect to the parcel data residing as a hosted feature layer on the GIS Hub's ArcGIS Online using ArcGIS Pro, then searching or browsing for and then selecting ' ndgishub parcels '. Please see Accessing Web Services and then expand the 'ArcGIS Online' section for detailed information. This access method performs very well when working in an agency office using a state-provided network connection or when working remotely where the network speed is relatively slow and/or when bandwidth may be restricted due to VPN software.
Using the Hub Data Portal in ArcPro
Data Access - Download
The parcel data is downloaded from the GIS Hub Data Portal. If you wish to browse to the data, select the ' Land Records ' theme and then scroll to 'NDGISHUB Parcels.' If you wish to search for the data simply enter the name (e.g., parcel) in the search box and then either wait for a moment to see the items to appear below the search box or press <enter> to see a full listing. Please note three parcel items will appear. The 'NDGISHub Parcels' is the "parent" of the data. Within that item, you will see the "children" or sub-items, 'Parcels' and 'Parcels_Taxroll.' Read the IMPORTANT items before scrolling down to the 'Parcels_TaxRoll' and 'Parcels' and clicking on those items.
Within the 'Parcels' or 'Parcels_Taxroll' item, click on the download icon (if present) and then click on the 'Download Zipped fGDB' or click on the Download button (if present) and then click on the 'Download Zipped fGDB. You may find using the 'Download Zipped fGDB' to expedite the download process. Please note that the zipped file contains an Esri file geodatabase containing both the parcel feature class and the tax roll table.
